title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect (Associate)
subtitle: Associate (SAA-C03)
offer_message: Limited Time Offer - Valid until Oct 25
description: This SAA-C03 practice test series is designed to help learners master core AWS architectural concepts through real exam-style scenarios. You’ll gain deep insights into designing resilient, fault-tolerant, and highly available systems on AWS. The course covers crucial domains such as security and compliance, cost-optimized architectures, operational excellence, and performance efficiency. Each question is accompanied by clear explanations and service comparisons, helping you understand the 'why' behind each answer. This is ideal for cloud engineers, developers, and architects preparing for the Associate-level exam.

sample_questions.question:
An ecommerce company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The workload currently consists of a web application and a backend Microsoft SQL database for storage. The company expects a high volume of customers during a promotional event. The new infrastructure in the AWS Cloud must be highly available and scalable.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
options: Migrate the web application to two Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server with read replicas in both Availability Zones.

Migrate the web application to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to two EC2 instances across separate AWS Regions with database replication.

Migrate the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment.

Migrate the web application to three Amazon EC2 instances across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to three EC2 instances across three Availability Zones.
sample_questions.explanation:
The correct answer is C

.

Option A (INCORRECT): Migrate the web application to two EC2 instances across two AZs behind an ALB and use RDS for SQL Server with read replicas in both AZs. Read replicas are intended for read-scaling and are not promoted automatically on primary failure—manual promotion adds administrative overhead. This setup does not provide automated failover for writes; you’d still have a single primary instance that could become a single point of failure. Maintaining read replicas across AZs increases complexity compared to a managed Multi-AZ deployment.

Option B (INCORRECT): Use an Auto Scaling group across two AZs for the web app and run two EC2 instances in separate AWS Regions with database replication. Cross-region replication increases network latency and costs, and adds complexity to failover processes. Managing SQL Server on EC2 instances requires patching, backups, monitoring and failover orchestration—high administrative overhead. This does not leverage RDS managed failover or scaling capabilities.

Option D (INCORRECT): Deploy three EC2 instances across three AZs for the app and three EC2 instances across three AZs for the database. Running SQL Server on EC2 means you must handle OS and database maintenance, backups, replication and failure recovery yourself. Provisioning and managing three database servers is complex and deviates from the “least administrative overhead” requirement. This approach ignores managed services like RDS that streamline HA and failover.

Option C (CORRECT): Migrate the web application to EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across two AZs behind an Application Load Balancer, and migrate the database to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment. Auto Scaling plus ALB provides automatic scaling and distribution of traffic for the web tier without manual intervention. RDS Multi-AZ ensures synchronous data replication, automatic failover, and managed backups—minimizing administrative tasks. This design meets high availability and scalability requirements while leveraging AWS managed services for the least overhead.

Summary: We evaluated four architectures and determined that only Option C leverages AWS managed services (Auto Scaling, ALB, RDS Multi-AZ) to provide high availability, scalability, and minimal administrative overhead.

reviews.comments: Excellent practice tests! Helped me identify weak areas and feel confident on exam day.

reviews.name: Sophia Lee
reviews.comments: Very realistic questions. Some explanations could be more detailed, but overall great value.
